Theming

The registry items ship no tokens of their own. Each one you copy in reads its colors from your app's Tailwind v4 @theme block. Re-theming your product never touches registry code. There is notailwind.config.js and no theme setting to configure.

This site reads its colors from one token sheet of plain CSS custom properties — no Tailwind, no @theme block. Every color in that sheet is an oklch value, and the dark values are the defaults. The sheet itself never reads your OSprefers-color-scheme setting. A script in the page head resolves your theme before first paint: your stored choice first, then your OS scheme, then dark.

The toggle in the site header is the live control. It flips alight class on the root element, and every token re-resolves in place — no reload, no second stylesheet.

The TextClassContext seam

React Native has no style cascade: a parent view cannot restyle the text inside a child component just by wrapping it. Registry parents that need to restyle nested text — message, prompt-input, tool, and the other list-bearing components — instead publish their class strings through the TextClassContext provider from the text module. Those class strings are ordinary Tailwind classes, so they resolve against your @theme block exactly like the classes you write yourself.

The renderMarkdown seam

The components that render model output — message, reasoning, context — do not bundle a markdown renderer. Each takes arenderMarkdown prop and defaults to plain text. The reference renderer, react-native-enriched-markdown, is a Fabric native module absent from Expo 57's bundled list; keeping it behind the prop is what leaves the core runnable in Expo Go, with markdown an opt-in step for dev-client apps.
